english.title: Send letter / communication / article conveying false information
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) sent to **(..SPECIFY PERSON..)

(A)_[a letter]_
(B)_[an electronic communication, namely **(..SPECIFY..),]_
(C)_[an article, namely **(..SPECIFY ARTICLE..),]_

which conveyed information which was false and which you knew or believed to be false for the purpose of causing distress or anxiety to the recipient or to any other person to whom you intended that it or its contents or nature should be communicated
english.legislation: Contrary to section 1(1)(a) and (4) of the Malicious Communications Act 1988.

english.notes:
(i) This offence no longer applies after 30th January 2024 due to changes made by the Online Safety Act 2023. For the offence of sending a false communication under section 179 of the Online Safety Act 2023, see H101561.
(ii) The "article" may be of any description.
(iii) The electronic communication may include text messages, fax and e-mail.
(iv) Consider section 127 of the Communications Act 2003 - offences regarding improper use of public electronic communications network and services. Although, note, the Online Safety Act 2023 also repeals those offences under section 127(2)(a) and (b) of the Communications Act 2003 (H5557 and H5558).
(iv) For offences committed prior to 13th April 2015, note that offences under section 1 of the Malicious Communications Act 1988 were 'summary only' and subject to a six month time limit for prosecutions.

other.penalty:
Summary: maximum 6/12 months imprisonment and / or a fine.
Indictment: maximum 2 years imprisonment and / or a fine.The maximum penalty on summary conviction may be 6 or 12 months depending on the general limit in a magistrates’ court, see section 282(2) and (3) of the Criminal Justice Act 2003 and section 224(1) and (1A) of the Sentencing Act 2022.

Time limit for prosecutions:
None
